facts.statement: The genus Pantosaurus was named by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1893.
Pantosaurus lived in the Sundance Sea, an ancient sea that once covered Wyoming.
facts.quote: It lived in what used to be the Sundance Sea.

facts.statement: The holotype of Pantosaurus is a partial articulated skeleton containing a distal humerus, four carpals, a coracoid fragment, and several cervical vertebrae from the Upper Member of the Sundance Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype YPM 543 is a partial articulated skeleton, partially prepared to yield a distal humerus, four articulated carpals, a fragment of the coracoid, and several isolated cervical vertebrae from the Upper Member of the Sundance Formation.

facts.statement: Muraenosaurus reedii is considered a junior synonym of Pantosaurus.
Pantosaurus possessed between 35 and 40 cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: Pantosaurus possesses between 35 and 40 cervical vertebrae

facts.statement: No skull or cranial material of Pantosaurus has been discovered yet.
facts.quote: No Pantosaurus cranial material has yet been discovered.

facts.statement: A partially digested embryonic ichthyosaur found inside a Pantosaurus fossil provided the first evidence that plesiosaurs consumed ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The discovery of a partially digested embryonic ichthyosaur (probably Baptanodon) inside of a fossil referable to Pantosaurus striatus was the first evidence of the consumption of ichthyosaurs by plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: Pantosaurus lived between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Oxfordian (161.5 to 154.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Pantosaurus belongs to the family Cryptoclididae.

rejected.statement: Pantosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic in what is now Wyoming.
rejected.quote: Pantosaurus ('all lizard') is an extinct genus of plesiosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) of what is now Wyoming.
